fundamental.text: Raw sugar is 2.03¢/lb above hydrous-ethanol parity in Brazil, so mills favour sugar in the mix (more supply). Sugar in BRL at R$2,298/t (57th pct of 5 yrs). The break below the 18c floor turned into a two-session slide, and Monday's bounce was short covering met by Brazilian mill and grower hedging on a weak real: the real channel is capping rallies while funds still hold a large net long. Desk read: Mar has extended to about 18.28 (+0.9%), back above its 100-day average, as the real firms close to 2% to ~5.82 per dollar, which further cuts Brazilian mills' appetite to hedge exports. There is still no fresh centre-south crush or mix data, and the surprise US tariff proposal on Brazil matters little for sugar flows, so the Brazil supply picture is unchanged and the move is currency and short covering.
